articles.title: Just a rumour of a bug is enough to find a security exploit these days
articles.selectionReason: AI source passed freshness and evidence-chain gate: GitHub
articles.summary: 本文报道了剑桥教授Anil Madhavapeddy的观察：OCaml项目的安全补丁一旦在公开讨论中分享，几分钟内就会出现自动化的漏洞探测尝试。rclone维护者也证实，近一个月收到的安全披露远超过去十年，且GitHub分配CVE的速度明显变慢。这说明现代编码代理已能基于极少量线索快速发现漏洞，开源社区现行的补丁保密与披露流程亟需重新设计。
articles.failureAnalysis: 这不是一个AI应用项目，而是对开源安全生态变化的警示。关键启示是：安全社区必须建立更快速的漏洞响应和披露机制，并借助AI工具进行漏洞分类与修复，才能应对攻击者自动化的速度。
articles.highlight: 补丁分享后约十分钟，相关网站就开始收到百分号编码遍历序列的探测，说明自动监控者正盯着公开仓库。
articles.sourceExcerpt: Just a rumour of a bug is enough to find a security exploit these days Anil Madhavapeddy is a professor of computer science at Cambridge and a core maintainer of the OCaml compiler. In this somewhat alarming post he reports that security issues in OCaml projects are seeing evidence of attempted exploits within minutes of patches being shared for discussion: This normally takes a few days and a release within a week or two is reasonable. Within about ten minutes (!) this website was fielding probes for percent-encoded traversal sequences, indicating that automated watchers are keeping an eye on public repositories.

zh.title: 一条bug传言，就足以让AI代理找到安全漏洞

en.summary: This article reports Cambridge professor Anil Madhavapeddy's observation that security patches in OCaml projects start receiving automated exploit probes within minutes of being shared publicly. The rclone maintainer confirms a dramatic surge in security disclosures, while GitHub's CVE assignment has slowed from days to weeks. It shows that modern coding agents can turn the slightest hint of a bug into an exploit, forcing open source communities to rethink their disclosure and patch-release processes.
en.failureAnalysis: This is not an AI application project but a warning about the changing security landscape. The key takeaway is that open source communities need faster vulnerability-response and disclosure workflows, and should leverage AI tools for triage and fixing to keep pace with automated attackers.
